assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean case of a theoretical prediction (a flat-band magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene) followed by experiments showing correlated insulators and superconductivity. It opened the broad field of moiré quantum matter and tunable correlated electrons, and its impact is large and still growing. This is the kind of discovery in nature that a theorist can respect: a concrete prediction that was tested.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group experiments are the decisive pair of contributions, so a theory-plus-experiment split is natural. Other experimental groups (for example on the correlated-insulator and superconducting phases) have a claim, so the three-person limit forces a judgement. The supplied credited names fit a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: The 2018 experiments have been reproduced by many independent groups and extended to related moiré systems, and the physical picture is stable. Eight years on, this is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include other experimental groups whose names are not in the credited list.
Several aspects of the superconducting mechanism remain debated, although the discovery itself is not.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (the magic-wavelength idea plus its realization) has delivered fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpins the coming redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. It is a clear invention with a clear measurable payoff, and it is original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated it; Ye's group pushed it to the best performance and to many-body, spin-exchange and clock-comparison physics. A two-person prize is clean. Other clock groups and the frequency-comb work (already honoured in 2005) are separate matters.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: several independent labs reproduce the performance, and the international metrology community is moving toward adoption.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Katori's proposal versus Ye's performance work, and whether the ion-clock community would argue for parallel recognition.
The overlap with the 2005 prize on precision spectroscopy and combs could be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect gave a new classification of electronic phases that is protected by symmetry. The theory (Kane-Mele) and the HgTe observation (Molenkamp) were a prediction tested in nature, and the concept spread through condensed matter, photonics and materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the decisive theorists. Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. That proposal and the three-dimensional materials (Bi2Se3, with Hasan and others) are not covered by these three names, so credit is not fully complete.
assessment.maturity: Mature: well over a decade of independent confirmation, and the topological classification is stable. The 2016 prize covers topological phase transitions and the TKNN-type physics, but the Z2 case is distinct enough.
uncertainties: Omission of Zhang and Bernevig-Hughes from the credit list and the three-dimensional topological insulator work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a conceptually original application of quantum mechanics (BB84, and E91 using entanglement and Bell's theorem). It links foundations to technology and has produced real networks and satellite links. I value that it is rooted in what Bell tests show in nature.
assessment.attribution: BB84 (Bennett, Brassard) and the E91 entanglement-based protocol (Ekert) form a natural trio. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known attribution wrinkle and cannot be recognized, as he is deceased.
assessment.maturity: Mature in principle with decades of experiments, though practical security (side channels) is still an engineering issue. The 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests partly overlaps, which affects timing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as physics or as information science.
Overlap with the 2022 prize and the Wiesner priority question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic plane signal, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. It is a genuine discovery in nature that opens a new window.
assessment.attribution: This is a large collaboration. Halzen is the leader and driving figure, with Karle and Spiering central to the construction and analysis. Credit also reaches earlier detector pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal, ANTARES), so a fair three-person split is difficult but the supplied names cover the leading figures.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established. Source identification is still at modest significance for individual sources, but the discovery itself is solid and has independent support from KM3NeT-type efforts.
uncertainties: Individual source associations remain partly statistical.
Collaboration-scale credit and the role of earlier neutrino-telescope pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Holography and AdS/CFT changed how we think about quantum gravity, black-hole information and strongly coupled field theory, and its conceptual weight is very large. As a string theorist I note frankly that it is still a theoretical correspondence, and the committee should look for clues in nature and not for beauty alone.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture is decisive. 't Hooft and Susskind formulated the holographic principle, and Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten gave the dictionary; those latter names are not in this entry. I propose Maldacena with Susskind, and 't Hooft is already a laureate (1999).
assessment.maturity: Applications to heavy-ion physics, condensed matter and quantum information give indirect support, but the correspondence has no direct empirical test in our universe and has not been rigorously proven. This is the weakest part of the case.
uncertainties: Lack of direct experimental confirmation and the role of AdS versus our de Sitter-like universe.
Credit distribution among Maldacena, Witten, Polyakov, Gubser, Klebanov, 't Hooft and Susskind.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the origin of primordial fluctuations, and the near scale-invariant, adiabatic and Gaussian spectrum seen in the CMB agrees with its predictions. Few ideas in cosmology have had such influence.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde (new inflation) and Mukhanov (quantum origin of fluctuations) are strong, but Starobinsky, Albrecht-Steinhardt and Chibisov are missing from the credit list, and the allocation is the most disputed part. Any three-person choice will be criticized.
assessment.maturity: The CMB supports the generic predictions, but there is no detection of primordial gravitational waves and alternatives are not decisively excluded. A prize for the specific mechanism could be premature.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Starobinsky and others.
No direct evidence for the inflaton or for primordial tensor modes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposals for quantum gates with trapped ions and for quantum simulation with cold atoms laid out how controllable quantum systems can compute and simulate many-body physics. The ideas have been realized in many laboratories and shaped the field.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theoretical originators of these proposals. A two-person theory prize would leave out the experimentalists who realized them; the Wineland/Haroche prize (2012) already recognized the ion and cavity manipulation.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many experiments, with growing practical relevance through quantum computing. Some of the field's recognition overlaps with the 2012 and 2022 prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes and whether a theory-only award is appropriate.
The balance between trapped-ion and neutral-atom contributions, and with experimental groups not credited here.
